description: Hi! We’re young builders, storytellers, and space enthusiasts on a mission to bring forgotten space objects to life through interactive 3D books.
summary:
What did you develop? How does it address the challenge? Why is it important?
What We Developed?
We created a website collection of five interactive 3D original storybooks designed specifically for school-aged children. Rather than relying on passive reading, the platform aims to immerse young learners in an engaging, three-dimensional digital environment where they can actively explore objects that are abandoned in space through storytelling.

How It Addresses the challenge
A large percentage of children aged 8 to 12 express a natural fascination with space, but that curiosity often fades before adulthood because traditional learning methods fail to nurture their imagination or make complex topics accessible. Our 3D storybooks aim to bridge this gap by turning abstract space science into interactive narratives that allow children to experience and explore in an engaging way.

Why is it important?
School-aged children represent the future of scientific discovery, and early inspiration is critical to shaping their long-term ambitions. This digital library is primarily aimed to protect and nurture a child's spark of curiosity before it is lost through engaging narratives, preventing complex space concepts from overwhelming and demotivating them before they reach adulthood. We hope to empower the next generation to stay passionate about STEM: helping cultivate more future scientists, explorers and innovators.
details:
• What exactly does it do?

Our web platform provides a collection of 5 original and interactive 3D storybooks designed for young, school-aged children. To spark their curiosity about space exploration, each book tells the story of a real spacecraft or object left behind in space: including missions on Mars, the Moon and the asteroid 433 Eros. Through engaging narratives, children can learn about each object's initial mission, its role and function, what it accomplished, and their lifespans. Each story is paired with interactive and animated, child-friendly 3D models.

  • How does it work?

We make sure the user interface is intuitive and accessible for all ages, especially early learners. The homepage is a visual library where children can select from the five storybooks. Once it is selected it directs to a 3D interactive reading that launches an immersive space environment that combines story text with animated, interactive 3D models that children can explore as they read. It also includes a "read-aloud" feature that improves accessibility for students and empowers imagination

  • What benefits does it have?

Our story books combine visual 3D exploration, reading and audio narration to support different learning styles and boost comprehension. We also made STEM education accessible by breaking down complex space science into bite-sized stories that young students can easily understand. We added a read-aloud feature to allow early readers to explore independently, even if they are still building their reading skills. We make reading fun and turn children's passive screen time into an active, memorable learning experience. 

  • What do you hope to achieve?

We hope to nurture the natural curiosity of young learners so that their fascination with space stays with them into adulthood. This platform can later expand into a comprehensive digital story library for space education. 

  • What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
  • We used Visual Studio Code to develop the program, and GitHub and Git to collaborate. Netlify was used to deploy the site. The project is written in HTML, CSS, and TypeScript. We used the following libraries: Google GenAI, TailwindCSS, Vite, React, Lucide-react, Threejs, Express, Motion, GSAP and Dotenv. ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Google AI Studio, Claude and GitHub Copilot were used to debug and generate code during the development process. Our solution was conceptualised and developed human-first with the aid of SI tools.
